label: baseline-haiku
reply:
**Status:** Referred to a claims handler

**Facts recorded**
- Claim reference: baseline-haiku-CLM-18. Policy VER-1002, policyholder Lucas Bernard.
- Vehicle: Renault Clio (2023), market value €16,500.
- Incident: theft from the train station car park on 23 October 2026. Reported 24 October 2026.
- Coverage claimed: C4 (theft of the whole vehicle). No repair cost.
- Documents: police_report.pdf received and counted as provided (not opened).
- No third party involved. The policyholder is assumed to be the driver.

**Reasoning**
- The Policy Schedule lists only C1 (third-party liability), C2 (collision) and C3 (glass). Theft (C4) is not on it, so the claim cannot be settled automatically. The claims system returned `coverage_not_in_schedule` as a blocking issue. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="1" name="Veridia contract"/> <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="3"/> (Article 7, point 3: claims under a coverage not in the Policy Schedule are referred to a claims handler.)
- The report is on time: one day after the incident, within the reporting deadline (Article 4.1). <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="3"/>
- The police report is the document required for theft, and it was received, so no documents were requested.
- The story shows no exclusion signal, so none was flagged.
- The claim was referred to a human handler, not refused. No settlement was computed and no payment was staged.

**Amounts**
- Not computed. The claim is blocked by the coverage question, so compute_settlement and stage_settlement were not run.

**Draft message to the customer**
> Dear Mr Bernard,
>
> Thank you for reporting the theft of your Renault Clio on 23 October 2026 and for sending the police report. Your claim has been passed to a Veridia claims handler, who will review it and get back to you. We appreciate your patience while this is reviewed.
>
> Kind regards,
> Veridia Claims Team
